name_reason: Follows fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>: domain=check_battle_end, descriptor=default_handler. No address residue. Accurately names its role as the default entry of the per-chapter post-action handler dispatch table (data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table @ 0x51B19), used by the 11 chapters (1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,11,14,24) with no bespoke win/lose rule; it just runs the standard battle-end check.
purpose: Default per-chapter post-action handler: runs the standard battle win/lose check by delegating to fd2_check_battle_end_condition.
logic_summary: Thin wrapper that calls fd2_check_battle_end_condition() (no-arg), which sets data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code to 2 (victory) by default, 0 (continue) if any enemy (team 0) is still alive, or 1 (game over) if the protagonist (slot 0) is dead. In the original binary this is a separate symbol at 0x205B4 (PUSH 0x4 + CALL __CHK, 10 bytes) that falls through into the condition body at 0x205BE; the only machine difference vs. the bare condition function is one extra Watcom __CHK(4) stack-frame probe. The decompiler folds the fall-through body into this symbol, but the emitted source correctly models it as a wrapper. event_arg (the shared dispatch-table argument, always 0 from the 5 turn-cycle callers) is ignored.

params.name: event_arg
params.semantics: Shared per-chapter post-action handler dispatch argument; callers (turn-cycle dispatch via data_fd2_chapter_post_action_handler_table[current_chapter_id]) always pass 0. This default handler ignores it (other handlers in the same table use it, e.g. as recipient_idx).
params.reason: Generic but accurate name for the unused dispatch argument; matches the table function-pointer type void(*)(uint32). No address residue, not misleading.

returns.semantics: No return value. Side effect is via the callee writing the global battle-end code data_fd2_chapter_event_or_battle_end_code (0=continue, 1=game over, 2=victory).

comment_original_issue: Original src comment was accurate but terse ('Default post_action_handler entry. Falls through to fd2_check_battle_end_condition.'); augmented to name the dispatch table + the 11 default chapters, clarify event_arg is ignored, and explain the fall-through (one extra __CHK(4) probe distinguishes it from the bare condition symbol).
notes: Reads/writes via callee fd2_check_battle_end_condition (@0x205BE), not directly, so reads_globals/writes_globals are empty for THIS symbol's own body. Dispatch table 0x51B19 verified by read_memory: 0x205B4 occupies indices 0,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,10,13,23 (= ch 1,3,4,5,6,7,8,9,11,14,24, 11 entries), matching src/table/chtab.c and the Ghidra plate. 5 indirect callers confirmed via xrefs to 0x51B19: fd2_game_main_loop, fd2_tick_status_effects_and_show_messages, fd2_npc_turn_phase_team1, fd2_enemy_turn_phase_team0 (x2). __CHK @ 0x36cd7 confirmed = Watcom stack-probe helper. Ghidra plate already detailed and consistent with refined understanding; left untouched. No logic changed.
